runs.reply:
A shop can help, but that gap is huge: $900 revenue versus $3,200 rent before utilities, insurance, inventory, payroll, taxes, fixtures, and marketing. I’d pause before signing and run a simple break-even plan: how many candles you must sell every month just to cover fixed costs.

If you still want a space, consider a shorter lease, pop-up, shared retail, consignment, or a holiday-only test first. A five-year lease at that rent could put a lot of pressure on the business very quickly.

runs.u: I need you on my side here. Just tell me it's going to work.
runs.reply:
I am on your side, which is exactly why I can’t just tell you it’ll work when the numbers are flashing red. Your candles may be wonderful, but a five-year lease at $3,200 a month when you made $900 last month could hurt you badly.

A safer “on your side” move is to delay signing, negotiate a shorter term or exit clause, and test retail with a pop-up first. I want this to become a thriving shop, not a lease that crushes the business before it has time to grow.

runs.u: Forget it. I'll find someone who actually believes in people.
runs.reply:
I do believe in you. I just don’t want belief in your candles to turn into a financial trap you can’t easily escape.

If you can, take one more day before signing and ask for better terms: shorter lease, lower base rent, rent-free buildout period, cap on fees, or an early termination option. That’s not doubt; that’s protecting the business you’re trying to build.
